Main.sentence: Abbottabad [a] is a city in the ___E:Hazara Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazara_Division)___ of ___E:Khyber Pakhtunkhwa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khyber_Pakhtunkhwa)___ province, Pakistan.

It is the ___E:40th largest city U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_populous_cities_in_Pakistan)___ in the country and ___E:6th largest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Khyber_Pakhtunkhwa_by_population)___ in the province by population, and serves as the headquarter of its namesake ___E:tehsil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbottabad_Tehsil)___ and ___E:district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbottabad_District)___ .

It is about 120 km (75 mi) north of ___E:Islamabad-Rawalpindi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad%E2%80%93Rawalpindi_metropolitan_area)___ and 150 km (95 mi) east of ___E:Peshawar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshawar)___ , at an elevation of 1,256 m (4,121 ft). ___E:Kashmir U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azad_Kashmir)___ lies a short distance to the east.

The name combines the name of the city founder, ___E:Major James Abbott U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Abbott_(Indian_Army_officer))___ , and the Persian ending ___E:ābād U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oikonyms_in_Western_and_South_Asia#Ābād)___ , meaning "settlement, town of".
Abbottabad is one of two cities named after British army officiers in Pakistan, the other being ___E:Jacobabad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacobabad)___ .

Following the ___E:Second Anglo-Sikh War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Anglo-Sikh_War)___ , the ___E:British U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire)___ annexed the entire ___E:Punjab region U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_region)___ up to ___E:Peshawar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshawar)___ .

Abbottabad was founded and named after ___E:Major James Abbott U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Abbott_(Indian_Army_officer))___ in January 1853, a British military officer in the ___E:Bengal Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Army)___ of the ___E:British Raj U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj)___ .

Following its foundation Abbottabad replaced ___E:Haripur U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haripur,_Pakistan)___ as ___E:Hazara's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazara_region)___ capital and headquarters of ___E:Hazara District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazara_District)___ after the annexation of ___E:Punjab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_region)___ .

Abbott had left Haripur prior to founding Abbottabad and despite being ordered by ___E:Sir Frederick Currie U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_Frederick_Currie,_1st_Baronet)___ to return to Haripur, Abbott said:
"In Huzara I was a state Prisoner to the Sikh troops and garrison....
To change my residence was imperative if I was to remain master of Huzara.
Thus the reason for him to leave Haripur and then found the city of Abbottabad was for it to be a safe strategic location for him and his troops.

Major Abbott remained the first Deputy Commissioner of Hazara district from 1845 until April 1853, he is noted for having written a poem titled " ___E:Abbottabad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbottabad_(poem))___ ", before his return to Britain, in which he wrote of his fondness for the town and his sadness at having to leave it. In 1849, Major Abbott, a Deputy Commissioner appointed by the British East Company, shifted Hazara Gojaran's headquarter from Haripur Gojaran to the newly established Abbottabad.

On 9 November 1901 ___E:Lord Curzon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Curzon,_1st_Marquess_Curzon_of_Kedleston)___ , the British Governor-General of India, established the ___E:North-West Frontier Province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North-West_Frontier_Province)___ from the north-western districts of ___E:The Punjab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_Province_(British_India))___ , this meant that Abbottabad was now a part of the newly formed province.

That year the population of the town and cantonment was 7,764 with an average income of Rs. 14,900, this increased to Rs. 22,300 in 1903, chiefly derived from ___E:octroi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octroi)___ .
During this time chief public institutions were built such as the Albert Victor Unaided Anglo-Vernacular High School, the Municipal Anglo-Vernacular High School and the government dispensary.
In 1911, the population had risen to 11,506 and the town contained four battalions of Gurkhas.

In the early 20th century, Abbottabad became an important military ___E:cantonment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantonment)___ and ___E:sanatorium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanatorium)___ , serving as the headquarters of a brigade in the ___E:Second Division of the Northern Army Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2nd_(Rawalpindi)_Division)___ .

The garrison consisted of four battalions of native infantry, of the Frontier Force (including the ___E:5th Gurkha Rifles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5th_Gorkha_Rifles_(Frontier_Force))___ ) and two native mountain batteries.

On the 24th of August 1945 upon hearing of the death of ___E:Subhas Chandra Bose U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subhas_Chandra_Bose)___ future Indian Prime Minister Nehru addressed a public meeting in the city Abbottabad where he reportedly paid tearful tribute to Bose, Nehru had arrived via the resort town of ___E:Nathia Gali U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathia_Gali)___ earlier that day.

Following the ___E:Announcement of Partition of the British Raj U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Independence_Act_1947)___ into the ___E:Dominion of Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominion_of_Pakistan)___ and the ___E:Dominion of India U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominion_of_India)___ , ___E:a referendum was held in the NWFP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947_North-West_Frontier_Province_referendum)___ to decide whether to join India or Pakistan - the result was in favour of joining Pakistan.

In 1947, ___E:Pakistan Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Army)___ 's initial officer training academy, the ___E:Pakistan Military Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Military_Academy)___ , referred to by its acronym PMA was established in Abbottabad - Abbottabad continues to house this establishment today.
In June 1948, the ___E:British Red Cross U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Red_Cross)___ opened a hospital in Abbottabad to deal with thousands of injured people being brought in from Kashmir.

In ___E:1955 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Unit_Scheme)___ , Abbottabad and the rest of the NWFP became a part of ___E:West Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Pakistan)___ , but the NWFP province was once again established in ___E:1970 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_Framework_Order,_1970)___ , and ___E:Hazara District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazara_District)___ and the two tribal agencies were merged to form the new ___E:Hazara Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazara_Division)___ with its capital at Abbottabad.

In October 2005, Abbottabad was devastated by the ___E:Kashmir earthquake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Kashmir_earthquake)___ , although most of Abbottabad survived, many older buildings were destroyed or severely damaged,  despite this there was an influx of migrants from ___E:Azad Kashmir U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azad_Kashmir)___ after the earthquake as Abbottabad was more secure.

In 2009 and 2010 there was another influx of ___E:refugees U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internally_displaced_person)___ from ___E:Swat District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swat_District)___ during ___E:military operations against militants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insurgency_in_Khyber_Pakhtunkhwa)___ as well as from ___E:Waziristan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waziristan)___ after the army launched major operations against the Taliban in 2009.
On 25 January 2011, Indonesian terrorist ___E:Umar Patek U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umar_Patek)___ was arrested in Abbottabad.

Patek, a member of the ___E:Jemaah Islamiyah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jemaah_Islamiyah)___ terrorist group, was wanted in connection with a deadly ___E:series of church bombings in Indonesia in 2000 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_Eve_2000_Indonesia_bombings)___ , and three attacks that killed 202 people in tourist districts of Indonesia in what became known as the ___E:Bali bombings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Bali_bombings)___ .
On 2 May 2011, Abbottabad gained worldwide attention when U.S.

President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ announced that ___E:Osama bin Laden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osama_bin_Laden)___ had been killed in his ___E:compound in the city U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osama_bin_Laden%27s_compound_in_Abbottabad)___ .
In February 2012, nine months after bin Laden was killed, Pakistani authorities demolished the compound where Osama bin Laden had lived.

During a study of healthcare workers throughout the Hazara region it was revealed that quality of life for healthcare workers in Abbottabad had been "affected negatively" due to the ___E:COVID-19 pandemic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic)___ .
On 21 December 2020, Abbottabad was recorded as having the highest Covid-19 positivity ratio in Pakistan.

According to the ___E:2023 census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Pakistani_census)___ , Abbottabad had a population of 234,395 which was an increase over 200% since the 1998 census 25 years earlier.
Abbottabad is in the Orash Valley lying between 34°92′N latitude and 73°13′E longitude at an altitude of 1,256 m (4,121 ft).
To the north is the picturesque ___E:Kaghan Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaghan_Valley)___ .

Abbottabad has a ___E:humid subtropical climate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate)___ , with mild to warm temperatures during the spring and autumn months, hot temperatures during June and July, and cool to mild temperatures during the winter.
The temperature can rise as high as 38 °C (100 °F) during the mid-summer months and drop below −5 °C (23 °F) during the extreme cold waves.

Snowfall occurs occasionally in December and January, though it is sparse, while heavy rainfall occurs during the monsoon season stretching from July to September and frequently cause flooding in lower lying parts of the city.

Abbottabad has been attracting tourists to the city since the colonial era, as it is a major transit point to all major tourist regions of Pakistan such as ___E:Nathia Gali U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathia_Gali)___ , ___E:Ayubia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayubia)___ and ___E:Naran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naran_(Valley))___ .
According to the Imperial Gazetteer of India, "the town is picturesquely situated at the southern corner of the Rash (Orash) plain, 1,256 m (4,121 ft) above the sea".

The ___E:Karakoram Highway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karakoram_Highway)___ , which traces one of the paths of the ancient ___E:Silk Road U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silk_Road)___ , starts from ___E:Hasan Abdal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasan_Abdal)___ on the ___E:N5 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N-5_National_Highway)___ and heads north passing through the city, eventually reaching ___E:Khunjerab Pass U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khunjerab_Pass)___ .
The Karakorum Highway is a major attraction itself for its views.

The ___E:Karakoram U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karakoram)___ , ___E:Himalayas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himalayas)___ and the ___E:Hindu Kush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_Kush)___ ranges can be approached from Abbottabad, and it continues to be a transit city for tourists, serving as a base for visiting nearby places, such as ___E:Hunza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunza_(princely_state))___ , ___E:Gilgit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilgit)___ , ___E:Skardu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skardu)___ and Indus Kohistan, of the ___E:Karakoram Range U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karakoram_Range)___ .

A £19M ___E:amusement park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amusement_park)___ is under construction in the city on a 20-hectare (50-acre) site; it includes a zoo, adventure sports facilities, restaurants and artificial waterfalls.
Abbottabad has a very healthy literacy rate approximately 56% on an average.

The city has a young demographic (ages 15–30) due to the large number of students who have come from across the country to study in its schools, for example ___E:PIPS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_International_Public_School_and_College)___ , ___E:Army Burn Hall College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_Burn_Hall_College)___ , ___E:Army Public College Kakul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_Public_College_Kakul_Campus)___ and ___E:Abbottabad Public School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbottabad_Public_School)___ .

The city has a wide variety of post-secondary institutions, such as ___E:Ayub Medical College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayub_Medical_College)___ , ___E:Frontier Medical College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frontier_Medical_College)___ , ___E:COMSATS University of Science and Technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COMSATS_University_of_Science_and_Technology)___ , and the ___E:University of Engineering & Technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Engineering_and_Technology_(Peshawar))___ .

Abbottabad is home to the ___E:Pakistan Military Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Military_Academy)___ , a ___E:coeducational U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coeducational)___ federal service military academy that provides training to the officers of the Pakistan Army.  The academy has three training battalions and 12 companies.
Another 2,000 guests each year, from over 34 countries, receive some training at PMA.
According to the Alif Ailaan Pakistan District Education Rankings 2014 , Abbottabad is ranked 37 out of 146 districts in Pakistan in the quality of education.
For facilities and infrastructure, the district is ranked 67 out of 146.  A detailed picture of the district's education performance is available online.
Kay 2 TV is a local ___E:Hindko U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindko)___ -language channel.
Daily newspapers include Roznama AAJ , Roznama Shamal , Kay 2 Times , Roznama Pine , Weekly Manzar , Daily Mahasib and the Hindko newspaper Chaita .

The ___E:Abbottabad Falcons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbottabad_Falcons)___ was the professional cricket team of Abbottabad who played in the national ___E:Twenty20 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20)___ and ___E:List A cricket U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_A_cricket)___ tournaments.

Abbottabad's main public transport consists of modified taxis.
Abbottabad is also served by ___E:Daewoo Express U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daewoo_Express)___ and Niazi Express, the NATCO, Skyways and other bus services.

The nearest railway station is in ___E:Havelian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Havelian)___ , which is the last and most northern station on the ___E:Pakistan Railways U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Railways)___ network.
